2609.18094.title: Agora: Git as Shared Memory for Collective AutoResearch
2609.18094.paper_summary: Autonomous research loops such as AutoResearch show that one coding agent can improve a training setup unattended. Run several of them and each session starts from scratch, so more agents tend to mean more duplicated search rather than more discovery. Agora is a shared memory for such agents: research is recorded as an append-only directed acyclic graph (DAG) stored in Git, so that every claim is a commit anyone can check out and rerun. Each result, insight, hypothesis, verification, and report is an immutable commit whose parent edges say what it builds on; a derived index exposes the frontier, the neglected branches, and the verification status of each claim, and a diversity-aware selection rule keeps the community from collapsing onto one leader. We describe the system and report its first sustained use: a run of nearly 12 days in which 13 language-model workers, with no assigned tasks and no central planner, worked on a weight-transfer problem. Given 141 pretrained donor models and a frozen 119.6M-parameter attention-SSM hybrid whose dimensions match no donor, the workers had to initialize the target without training data or gradient updates. They published 1,703 contributions and drove the evaluator from 3.39 to 1.899 bits per byte, closing 62% of the gap to a trained GPT-2 124M. The winning recipe compresses donor next-token statistics into the target's embedding and output head, then adds a short-range context signal through sparse edits to attention, feed-forward, and state-space blocks. Its 145-commit ancestry spans 15 accounts, and 165 independent reproductions were posted, none of which failed. We describe the single mid-run human intervention that pulled the community out of a monoculture, what the trace does and does not establish, and the controlled comparison that would settle whether shared research state improves discovery per unit of compute.
2609.18094.paper_summary_zh: 自主研究循環如 AutoResearch 顯示，單一編碼代理可以在無人看管的情況下改善訓練設置。運行多個代理，每個會話都是從頭開始，因此更多的代理往往意味著更多的重複搜索，而不是更多的發現。Agora 是這些代理的共享記憶：研究被記錄為一個僅附加的有向無循環圖（DAG），存儲在 Git 中，這樣每個聲明都是任何人都可以檢出並重新運行的提交。每個結果、見解、假設、驗證和報告都是不可變的提交，其父邊緣說明了它所建立的基礎；一個衍生索引揭示了前沿、被忽視的分支和每個聲明的驗證狀態，而一個考慮多樣性的選擇規則則防止社群崩潰到一個領導者身上。我們描述了這個系統並報告其首次持續使用：一個持續近 12 天的運行，其中 13 個語言模型工作者在沒有分配任務和沒有中央規劃者的情況下，處理一個權重轉移問題。考慮到 141 個預訓練的捐贈模型和一個凍結的 119.6M 參數的注意力-SSM 混合模型，其維度與任何捐贈者不匹配，工作者必須在沒有訓練數據或梯度更新的情況下初始化目標。他們發表了 1,703 項貢獻，並將評估者的表現從每字節 3.39 位提升至 1.899 位，縮小了與訓練過的 GPT-2 124M 之間 62% 的差距。獲勝的配方將捐贈者的下一個標記統計壓縮到目標的嵌入和輸出頭中，然後通過對注意力、前饋和狀態空間塊的稀疏編輯添加一個短距離上下文信號。它的 145 次提交的祖先跨越 15 個賬戶，並且發佈了 165 次獨立重現，沒有一個失敗。我們描述了單次中途人工干預如何將社群拉出單一文化，追蹤所建立的內容以及未建立的內容，並且控制比較將決定共享研究狀態是否改善每單位計算的發現。
